source_checks.finding: Page confirms: 'If the printer isn't found automatically, next to The printer that I want isn't listed, select Add a new device manually.' and 'In the Add Printer window that opens, follow the instructions.' The page lists Windows 11 and Windows 10 as separate tabs, so the Windows 11 applicability holds. Only applies when the printer does not appear in the list, as the ref states.

Same page. Page confirms: 'Make sure the printer is plugged into the Windows device, for example via USB, and that the printer is turned on.' 'Select Start > Settings > Bluetooth & devices > Printers & scanners.' 'Check if the printer is already installed in the list of installed printers.' 'If the printer isn't installed, go to Add a printer & scanner and then select Add device.' 'It might take a few minutes for the list of printers to finish populating.' 'Select the Add Device button next to the desired printer.' Also 'For wireless printers, make sure the printer is on the same wireless network as the Windows device.' Covers Windows 11 and USB/local printers, as the ref states.

required_actions.action: Make sure the printer is turned on and connected to the PC (for example by USB), or on the same network if wireless
Open Start > Settings > Bluetooth & devices > Printers & scanners
Check the installed list for the printer (already completed by the user, who says it is not listed)
Go to Add a printer & scanner and select Add device, then wait for the list to populate
If the printer still does not appear, select Add a new device manually next to The printer that I want isn't listed
Follow the instructions in the Add Printer window that opens
